hero.title: A list of people who said yes
hero.body: Professionals who have agreed to answer questions from your students about their job, their route in, and what the work is actually like. Register the school and your guidance counsellor gets the full directory. There is no charge.

how.title: What a school gets
how.body: A guidance counsellor registers, gets a login, and browses the directory. If you want somebody to come in and talk, you email us and we sort it. That is the entire process and there is nothing else to learn.

items.title: Names, not job descriptions
items.body: Professionals across every sector, from people three years out of school to people running the place. Searchable by industry and by how long they have been at it.

items.title: Somebody standing in front of a class
items.body: A whole year group, or six students with a specific interest. Email us and we find the person and organise it. You do not fill in a form.

items.title: Junior and senior, and the junior ones matter more than you'd think
items.body: Someone fifteen years in brings the wider view. Someone three years in is close enough that a student believes them. The second is harder to find and more useful than it sounds.

items.title: Nobody's phone number changes hands
items.body: Mentors' personal contact details are not visible to you or to your students. They sit in a separate place only we can open, and we make the introductions. That is on purpose.

items.title: After they leave, it keeps going
items.body: Once a former student is over 18 they can get their own account and contact mentors directly. That is when an internship is actually at stake, and it is the part nobody else does.

cta.title: Registering
cta.body: A few minutes, and then your guidance counsellor has the lot. No trial, no tier, no invoice arriving in March.

founding.line: The first 10 schools to join are founding schools. Free, permanently, and named on this site. After that it's €200 a year — and free to any school where cost is genuinely the barrier. Just say so.

facts.line: More than 900 DEIS schools in Ireland and roughly 160,000 students in them.
